turn.subject: solution
turn.user_message: Show me how we’ll know it worked

text: We’ll watch a short list of numbers, week by week. Where you already gave me a number, that is where we start. Why these:
bullets: They measure the wait itself, not how busy people are, so a busy week can’t hide a slow one.
They start from your own numbers, so progress is measured against you, not against other hospitals.
Nothing tracks some of them today. Those are marked new, and the first week of the trial gives their starting number.
chat.invite: That’s all five parts. Shall I put them into a plan, starting with a short trial?
chat.note: Measure the wait, not the effort.

points.label: Decisions made on the evening round

prompts: Yes — put it into a plan
Who reports these numbers each week?
What counts as a good result?

items.title: Hours from ready to home
more_points: From the doctor saying the patient can go, to the patient leaving the building.
Counted for every patient, not a sample.
Reported every week, ward by ward.

items.title: Home by 10 AM
items.text: Goal: patients paying themselves home by 10 AM, 11 at the latest. Insured patients by 1 PM.
more_points: The share of each day’s patients who have left by those times.
No starting number yet. The first week of the trial sets it.

items.title: Decided on the evening round
items.text: The share of going-home decisions made at 7 PM.
more_points: It shows whether the evening is really being used. That is the heart of the fix.
The software records it by itself, so nobody fills in a form.

items.title: Insurance approval time
items.text: How long the insurer takes, in the evening and in the morning.
more_points: It shows whether sending the first bill overnight is working.
The insurer is outside your control, so this is kept apart from your own delays.

items.title: Bed ready for the next patient
items.text: Time from the patient leaving to the bed being ready again.
more_points: Includes the wait before housekeeping is told, not only the cleaning.
Checked against the bed desk’s own times.

items.title: Money won back
items.text: Freed beds given to new patients, against the ₹10.3 crore a year at stake.
more_points: Only beds that are really filled again count, not beds that are just freed.
The new roles pay for themselves at about 1% of this.

stats.label: Measures with a starting number
stats.note: the trial’s first week sets the rest
